summary: Feature Flags system tested end-to-end (backend + frontend). Public catalog, admin CRUD (partial), 503 guards on POST /ads, /special-tasks, /marketplace, empty-list on GET /ads when OFF, persistence across supervisor restart, frontend landing gate, admin toggle UI (9 rows/toggles), FeatureGuard placeholders on protected user routes. 13/15 backend tests PASS. 1 CRITICAL SECURITY BUG found: /api/admin/feature-flags GET & PUT are accessible WITHOUT authentication (returns 200 to anyone; anyone on the internet can list AND toggle flags). All flags left OFF at the end of testing.

critical.issue: Endpoint accessible without any Authorization header — returns 200 with full flag list to unauthenticated callers. Also returns 200 to non-admin authenticated users.

Endpoint accepts flag toggles WITHOUT auth. Verified via curl: `curl -X PUT .../api/admin/feature-flags/paid_tasks -d '{"enabled":false}'` returned 200 with no token. This lets anyone on the internet disable/enable production features.

issues: Missing data-testid on email/password inputs and submit button (login-email-input / login-password-input / login-submit-btn). Not a blocker but hurts test automation.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix admin auth on feature-flags router. Root cause: `ff_admin.dependencies.append(_Depends(require_admin))` in /app/backend/server.py:3298 mutates the router.dependencies list AFTER the @admin.get/put decorators registered the routes with the (empty) dependencies snapshot — the mutation is not applied to those routes. Fix: declare the router with `admin = APIRouter(prefix='/api/admin', tags=['admin-features'], dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])` inside feature_flags.py (or pass `dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)]` to `app.include_router(ff_admin, ...)` in server.py). Verified with curl that unauthenticated GET & PUT return 200.
Nice-to-have: add data-testid to login form inputs & submit button.
critical_code_review_comments: SECURITY: Admin feature-flag endpoints exposed without auth (see action items).

server.py line 3298: mutating `ff_admin.dependencies` after decoration doesn't propagate to already-registered routes in FastAPI — this is a subtle FastAPI foot-gun. Prefer declaring dependencies on APIRouter constructor.

rca_of_the_issue.bug: GET/PUT /api/admin/feature-flags accessible without auth (401/403 expected, 200 returned)
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: curl -sX GET https://jobs-badges-fix.preview.emergentagent.com/api/admin/feature-flags -w '%{http_code}'  → 200 + full items list. curl -sX PUT .../api/admin/feature-flags/paid_tasks -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"enabled":false}' → 200.
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: In /app/backend/server.py:3290-3300, the feature_flags admin router is imported with NO dependencies, then `ff_admin.dependencies.append(_Depends(require_admin))` is called. In FastAPI, decorator calls (@admin.get(...), @admin.put(...)) register each Route with a snapshot of the router's dependencies AT DECORATION TIME. Later mutations of `router.dependencies` do not retroactively affect already-registered routes. So the append is a no-op for security purposes.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: In /app/backend/feature_flags.py line ~89, change `admin = APIRouter(prefix='/api/admin', tags=['admin-features'])` to `admin = APIRouter(prefix='/api/admin', tags=['admin-features'], dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])` (and import Depends + require_admin). Remove the append hack in server.py. Alternative: use `app.include_router(ff_admin, dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])`.
